The first public beta of Oculibre: your Android phone becomes the webcam of your computer, over the
Wi-Fi (encrypted) or the USB cable. Free, open source, no account, nothing leaves your network.

## Download

| Your device | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 11 or 10 (64-bit) | `Oculibre_0.4.0_x64-setup.exe` |
| Ubuntu 26.04 | `Oculibre_0.4.0_ubuntu-26.04_amd64.deb` |
| Ubuntu 24.04 | `Oculibre_0.4.0_ubuntu-24.04_amd64.deb` |
| Debian 13 | `Oculibre_0.4.0_debian-13_amd64.deb` |
| Android 5.0 and up | `Oculibre_0.4.0_android.apk` |

Check a download with `SHA256SUMS.txt` (`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`).
How to start: see the [README](https://github.com/Raspeur/Oculibre#get-started).

## What works

- **Every app sees the phone as a webcam** named "Oculibre": OBS, Zoom, Teams, Discord, Google
  Meet, browsers; on Windows 11 also the Windows Camera app.
- **Wi-Fi**, encrypted (TLS), after pairing once with a QR code; the phone then finds the computer
  by itself. **USB**, with USB debugging on the phone.
- **Picture**: every camera of the phone, only the modes it really delivers, up to 1080p at 60 fps
  or 4K; follows the phone's rotation; mirror on demand. About 80 ms of delay at 1080p60.
- **Desktop app** in English and French: live preview, camera and quality chosen from the computer,
  settings remembered for each phone, tray icon, start with the computer, guided tour, clear
  messages with a code when something needs attention.
- **Linux**: the virtual camera is set up by the package, Secure Boot included (Debian asks to
  enroll a key once). **Windows**: decoding on the graphics card, no runtime to install.

## Known limits

- **USB needs USB debugging** (Developer options), which gives the computer wide access to the
  phone: allow only your own computer. A version without it is planned (#21). Wi-Fi does not need it.
- **The Windows installer is not signed yet**: Windows SmartScreen shows "Unknown publisher"; choose
  "More info" then "Run anyway".
- On Windows 11 a second camera appears, "Oculibre" followed by "Windows Virtual Camera" in your
  language: it serves one app at a time. To use several apps at once, choose the plain "Oculibre".
- Some phone makers stop background apps (Xiaomi MIUI, others): the app shows how to allow it.
- No sound yet, no macOS (#19). Other Linux distributions: build from source.

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra (Android 17) and a Xiaomi Redmi Note 9 Pro (Android 12), with
Ubuntu 26.04 and 24.04, Debian 13, Windows 11 and 10. Your phone is not in the list? A
[device report](https://github.com/Raspeur/Oculibre/issues/new?template=device_report.yml) helps a lot.
